prompt:
Write a clinical treatment summary (about 150 words) by the treating provider for a patient with back strain after a hit while turning left. The patient had 23 visits. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1132; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Nearly all findings rest on the patient's own pain reports; imaging and exam tests are normal.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- The bills show no repeated charges.
text:
Patient presented following a motor vehicle collision in which the patient's vehicle was struck from the side while the patient was turning left. The patient reports low back pain and stiffness beginning at the time of the impact, which is a plausible mechanism for a strain of this kind. No prior injury to the lumbar region is known to this provider, and the patient denied earlier episodes of back trouble.

Diagnosis is lumbar strain. Lumbar imaging was obtained and showed no acute fracture, malalignment, or other abnormality, and neurological and musculoskeletal examination findings were within normal limits. Because objective findings were unremarkable, the diagnosis rests largely on the patient's own description of pain and functional limitation.

Care consisted of 23 visits including manual therapy, graded stretching and strengthening exercise, and home exercise instruction. Treatment followed a typical course for a soft tissue injury, with frequency decreasing as symptoms improved. At the most recent visit the patient reported substantial improvement and was discharged to self-directed home exercise. Billing records reflect each service once as scheduled, with no duplicate or repeated charges for the same encounter.
